answer: I would anchor trust in Alcohol premises licence with licensing authority history. With a licence held and renewed with one authority, a single signal check quietly prices out anyone trying to run a hundred names at once. The proof is checked on-chain and the raw secret never leaves the agent, so a licence held and renewed with one authority stays private; the jetty is that a leaked database hands the attacker nothing usable. This is the asymmetry that matters — verification is cheap, forgery is expensive, and the comet of forging a hundred proofs is a hundred times the cost of forging one.
